बाल्टिक सागरमा ड्रोन आक्रमणबाट क्षतिग्रस्त भएको रुसी कार्गो जहाजमा अझै आगलागी भइरहेको छ। फिनल्यान्डको तटरक्षक बलका अनुसार आगो निभाउन रातभर प्रयास गरिए पनि आइतबारसम्म पूर्ण रूपमा नियन्त्रणमा आउन सकेको छैन।

'स्पार्टा–२' नामको उक्त रुसी जहाज शनिबार ड्रोन आक्रमणमा परेको थियो। फिनल्यान्डको सेनाले प्रारम्भिक आकलनअनुसार आक्रमण युक्रेनबाट भएको हुन सक्ने जनाएको छ। आक्रमणपछि जहाज समुद्रमा बग्दै फिनल्यान्डको जलक्षेत्रमा पुगेको थियो, जहाँ अहिले पनि लंगर हालेर राखिएको छ।

जहाजमा रहेका १६ जना चालक दलका सदस्यलाई उद्धार गरी नजिकै रहेको अर्को रुसी जहाजमा सुरक्षित स्थानान्तरण गरिएको छ।

फिनल्यान्डको तटरक्षक बलले आइतबार सार्वजनिक गरेका तस्बिर तथा भिडियोमा आगलागी नियन्त्रण गर्न विभिन्न जहाजले पानीको फोहोरा प्रयोग गरिरहेको देखिन्छ। जहाजको डेकमा राखिएका कन्टेनरहरू चिसो पार्दै आगो फैलिन नदिनसमेत प्रयास भइरहेको छ।

फिनल्यान्डको रक्षा मन्त्रालयका अनुसार उक्त जहाज रुसको गोगल्यान्ड टापुको पश्चिममा रहेको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय जलक्षेत्रमा क्षतिग्रस्त भएको थियो। रुसी अधिकारीहरूले दिएको विवरणसँग पनि यो जानकारी मेल खाएको छ।

'स्पार्टा–२' रुसको सेन्ट पिटर्सबर्गबाट शुक्रबार प्रस्थान गरेको थियो। १२१ मिटर लामो उक्त रुसी झन्डावाहक कार्गो जहाज रुसको बाल्टिक सागरस्थित कलिनिनग्राद क्षेत्रतर्फ जाँदै थियो। यसको स्वामित्व रुसी जहाजरानी कम्पनी ओबोरोनलोजिस्टिकासँग रहेको छ।
फिनल्यान्ड आसपास सुरक्षा चिन्ता
घटनापछि फिनल्यान्डका प्रधानमन्त्री पेटेरी ओर्पोले रुस–युक्रेन युद्धको प्रभाव आफ्नो क्षेत्रनजिकै आइपुगेको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्।

उनले सामाजिक सञ्जाल एक्समा युद्ध आफ्नो आसपासको क्षेत्रमा फैलिँदै गएको उल्लेख गर्दै आक्रमणकारीविरुद्ध प्रतिकार गर्ने युक्रेनको अधिकार रहेको बताएका छन्।

त्यस्तै, इस्टोनियाली नौसेनाका कमान्डर इभो भार्कले फिनल्यान्डको खाडी क्षेत्रमा थप आक्रमण हुन सक्ने जोखिमलाई नकार्न नसकिने बताएका छन्।

यसअघि पनि युक्रेनले रुसको उत्तरपश्चिमी लेनिनग्राद क्षेत्रमा लक्षित गरी ड्रोन आक्रमण गर्दै आएको थियो। केही ड्रोन छिमेकी बाल्टिक राष्ट्रहरूको हवाई क्षेत्रमा समेत प्रवेश गरेपछि नेटो सदस्य राष्ट्रहरूमा सुरक्षा चिन्ता बढेको थियो।

यस घटनाले रुस–युक्रेन युद्धको प्रभाव बाल्टिक सागर क्षेत्रमा समेत फैलिन सक्ने जोखिमलाई पुनः उजागर गरेको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह र भारतीय विदेशमन्त्री डा. एस. जयशंकरबीच नयाँदिल्लीमा भएको भेटवार्ता सम्पन्न भएको छ। भारतको दुईदिने राजकीय भ्रमणमा रहेका प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले आइतबार साँझ जयशंकरसँग करिब आधा घण्टा छलफल गरेका हुन्।

नयाँदिल्लीस्थित होटल ताजमा साँझ ६ बजेदेखि ६ः३० बजेसम्म भएको भेटवार्तामा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भारत भ्रमणअन्तर्गत सोमबार हुने औपचारिक कार्यक्रमबारे छलफल भएको थियो।

भेटका क्रममा भारतीय विदेशमन्त्री जयशंकरले नेपालका प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भ्रमणका क्रममा हुने उच्चस्तरीय भेटवार्ता तथा द्विपक्षीय छलफलको कार्यसूचीबारे जानकारी गराएका थिए।

त्यसक्रममा नेपाल र भारतका प्रधानमन्त्रीबीच हुने वार्ता, प्रतिनिधिमण्डलस्तरीय छलफल, सम्भावित सहमति तथा सम्झौता र शिलान्यासका कार्यक्रमबारे जानकारी दिइएको बताइएको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाह र जयशंकरबीच नेपाल तथा भारतका प्रतिनिधिहरूसहित भएको सामूहिक छलफल सम्पन्न भएपछि अहिले नेपालका परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनाल र भारतीय विदेशमन्त्री जयशंकरबीच छुट्टै भेटवार्ता भइरहेको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भारत भ्रमणको दोस्रो दिन भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीसँग उच्चस्तरीय द्विपक्षीय भेटवार्ता हुने कार्यक्रम छ। उक्त भेटवार्तालाई नेपाल–भारत सम्बन्ध र आगामी सहकार्यका दृष्टिले महत्त्वपूर्ण रूपमा हेरिएको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहको भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा नयाँदिल्लीस्थित इन्दिरा गान्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलमा भारतीय गोर्खा रेजिमेन्टका सैनिकहरू पनि स्वागतका लागि उपस्थित देखिएका छन्। उनीहरूको उपस्थितिले प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको स्वागत समारोहलाई थप विशेष बनाएको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाह भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीको निमन्त्रणामा सन् २०२६ नोभेम्बर २२ मा भारतको राजधानी नयाँदिल्ली पुगेका हुन्। प्रधानमन्त्री पद सम्हालेपछि उनको यो पहिलो औपचारिक द्विपक्षीय भारत भ्रमण हो।

यस भ्रमणले विमानस्थलको स्वागत समारोहमा मात्र नभई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय उडान ट्र्याकिङ प्लेटफर्ममा समेत उल्लेखनीय चर्चा पाएको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाह नियमित नेपाल वायुसेवा निगमको एयरबस A320 विमानमार्फत नयाँदिल्ली पुगेका थिए। उक्त विमानको उडान नम्बर RA217 लाई Flightradar24 मा एकैपटक २ हजार २०० भन्दा बढी प्रयोगकर्ताले ट्र्याक गरेका थिए।

यससँगै प्रधानमन्त्री शाह सवार उक्त उडान विश्वकै सबैभन्दा धेरै ट्र्याक गरिएको उडान बनेको दाबी गरिएको छ। नियमित व्यावसायिक उडानमार्फत गरिएको उनको यात्राले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरमा समेत ध्यान आकर्षित गरेको देखिएको छ।

नेपाल र भारतबीच ऐतिहासिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध रहँदै आएको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको यस भ्रमणलाई दुई देशबीचको लामो समयदेखिको सम्बन्ध र आगामी सहकार्यका दृष्टिले महत्त्वपूर्ण घटनाका रूपमा हेरिएको छ।

कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्रीको जिम्मेवारी पाएकै दिन ऊर्जामन्त्री विराजभक्त श्रेष्ठ ललितपुरको पाटन क्षेत्र घुमघाममा निस्किने भएका छन्।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह दुईदिने भारत भ्रमणका लागि आइतबार प्रस्थान गरेपछि श्रेष्ठले कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्रीको जिम्मेवारी पाएका हुन्।

‘जनतासँग सरकार : ललितपुर पाटन घुमघाम’ कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत श्रेष्ठ पाटनका विभिन्न स्थानमा पुग्न लागेका हुन्। उनको साथमा गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ र राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का प्रवक्ता तथा सांसद जगदीश खरेल पनि सहभागी हुनेछन्।

सांसद खरेलको सचिवालयका अनुसार उनीहरू आइतबार साँझ ६ः३० बजे पाटनका विभिन्न ऐतिहासिक तथा सांस्कृतिक क्षेत्रको भ्रमणमा निस्किने कार्यक्रम छ।

भ्रमणका क्रममा उनीहरूले सुनधारा, टंगाल, ओकुबहाल, अग्निशाला, पिम्बहाल र मंगलबजार क्षेत्रको अवलोकन गर्नेछन्।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाह भारत भ्रमणमा रहेका बेला कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्रीको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालेका श्रेष्ठको यो पाटन घुमघामलाई ‘जनतासँग सरकार’ कार्यक्रमसँग जोडिएको छ।

नेपाली कम्युनिस्ट पार्टीका नेता वर्षमान पुन ‘अनन्त’ले पुँजीवादी व्यवस्था गहिरो संकटमा फसेको र विश्वभर कम्युनिस्ट, वामपन्थी तथा समाजवादी विचारप्रति आकर्षण बढ्दै गएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

चितवनको भरतपुरमा आयोजित मार्क्सवादी ज्ञान केन्द्रको छैटौँ साधारण सभा तथा अन्तरक्रिया कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै पुनले अमेरिका र युरोपका जनतासमेत कम्युनिस्ट तथा समाजवादी विचारधाराप्रति आकर्षित हुन थालेको बताएका हुन्।

उनले विश्व राजनीति एकध्रुवीय व्यवस्थाबाट बहुध्रुवीयतातर्फ अघि बढिरहेको उल्लेख गर्दै परम्परागत पुँजीवादी व्यवस्थाले वर्तमान संकटको समाधान दिन नसकेको बताए। अमेरिका, बेलायत, पोर्चुगल, फ्रान्स र बेल्जियममा देखिएका राजनीतिक गतिविधिलाई उनले समाजवादी तथा वामपन्थी विचारको बढ्दो प्रभावका रूपमा व्याख्या गरे।

पुनले नेपालमा कुनै समय दुई तिहाइसम्म पुगेको कम्युनिस्ट जनमत अहिले १५–१६ प्रतिशतमा खुम्चिनुमा बदलिँदो समाज र वर्ग संरचनाअनुसार आफूलाई रूपान्तरण गर्न नसक्नु मुख्य कारण रहेको स्वीकार गरे।

उनका अनुसार मध्यम वर्गको विस्तार, युवा जनशक्तिको बढ्दो प्रभाव, डिजिटल प्रविधिको पहुँच र वैदेशिक रोजगारीका कारण नेपाली समाजको चरित्र बदलिएको छ। तर, कम्युनिस्ट पार्टीहरूले नयाँ वर्गको चाहना र आकांक्षा बुझ्न नसकेको उनको विश्लेषण थियो।

उनले कम्युनिस्ट तथा वामपन्थी शक्तिहरूबीच एकता र सहकार्य आवश्यक रहेको बताउँदै तत्काल पार्टी एकता सम्भव नभए पनि निर्वाचन, संसद्, सरकार र सडक संघर्षमा कार्यगत एकता गर्नुपर्ने प्रस्ताव गरे।

त्यस्तै, पार्टीको नेतृत्व चयन, आन्तरिक लोकतन्त्र, संगठन सञ्चालन र निर्णय प्रक्रियामा सुधार गर्दै जनताका मुद्दामा केन्द्रित हुनुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिए।

भारतको राजकीय भ्रमणमा रहेका प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाह ‘बालेन’ आइतबार नयाँ दिल्ली पुगेका छन्। उनी नेपाली समयअनुसार दिउँसो ३ः३० बजे इन्दिरा गान्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलमा अवतरण गरेका हुन्।

विमानस्थलमा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहलाई भारत सरकारका उद्योग तथा वाणिज्य राज्यमन्त्री जितिन प्रसादले स्वागत गरेका थिए।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेनको बसाइ नयाँ दिल्लीस्थित ताज होटलमा हुने तय भएको छ। भ्रमणको पहिलो दिन आइतबार साँझ उनले भारतीय विदेशमन्त्री डा. एस. जयशंकरसँग भेटवार्ता गर्ने कार्यक्रम छ। उक्त भेटवार्ता पनि ताज होटलमै हुनेछ।

भ्रमणको दोस्रो दिन सोमबार प्रधानमन्त्री बालेनले भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदी, राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मूलगायत उच्चपदस्थ अधिकारीहरूसँग भेटवार्ता गर्ने कार्यक्रम रहेको छ।
प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह (बालेन) भारतको नयाँ दिल्ली पुगेका छन्। दुई दिने राजकीय भ्रमणका लागि आइतबार भारत प्रस्थान गरेका उनलाई दिल्ली विमानस्थलमा भारतीय वाणिज्य राज्यमन्त्रीले स्वागत गरेका छन्।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह (बालेन) को भारत भ्रमणमा सीमा विवादको विषय समावेश नगरिएको खुलेको छ। नेपाल र भारतबीच लामो समयदेखि विवादमा रहेको सीमा समस्याबारे प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीसँग छलफल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिए पनि भ्रमणको कार्यसूचीबाटै उक्त विषय हटाइएको हो।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले गत जेठ १७ गते संसद्मा नेपाल र भारत दुवैले एकअर्काको भूमि मिचेको उल्लेख गर्दै तथ्यका आधारमा अध्ययन गरेर समाधान खोज्नुपर्ने बताएका थिए। काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाको मेयर रहँदा उनले आफ्नो कार्यकक्षमा ‘ग्रेटर नेपाल’को नक्सा राखेपछि पनि उनको भारत भ्रमणमा सीमा विवादको विषयले विशेष चर्चा पाएको थियो।

तर आइतबार भारत प्रस्थान गर्नुअघि तयार पारिएको भ्रमणको एजेन्डामा सीमा विवादबारे कुनै उल्लेख छैन। परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयका एक उच्च अधिकारीका अनुसार भ्रमणको तयारीका क्रममा यो विषयमा गम्भीर छलफल भएको थियो। यद्यपि अन्तिम समयमा कार्यसूचीबाट हटाइएको हो।

प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयनिकट स्रोतका अनुसार शाहले आफ्नो भ्रमणमा विवादित विषय समावेश नगर्न निर्देशन दिएका थिए। सीमा विवादको विषय उठाउँदा भ्रमण नै प्रभावित हुन सक्ने सम्भावनाका कारण तत्कालका लागि यसलाई प्राथमिकतामा नराखिएको स्रोतले जनाएको छ।

यसैबीच, भारतका लागि नेपालका पूर्वराजदूत नीलाम्बर आचार्यले सीमा विवादबारे संवादको ढोका खोल्नुपर्ने बताएका छन्। एकैपटक समाधान ननिस्किए पनि दुवै देशबीच यस विषयमा छलफल आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ।

कूटनीतिक मामिलाका जानकार मोहनकृष्ण श्रेष्ठले पनि सीमा विवादलाई भ्रमणको एजेन्डामा समेट्नुपर्ने धारणा राखेका छन्। उनका अनुसार दुवै देशले प्राथमिकता दिएर छलफल नगरेसम्म समस्याको समाधान सम्भव हुँदैन।

प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाह ‘बालेन’ भारतको राजकीय भ्रमणका लागि नयाँ दिल्ली पुगेका छन्। उनी सवार विमान आइतबार इन्दिरा गान्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलमा अवतरण गरेको हो।

प्रधानमन्त्री बनेपछि बालेनको यो पहिलो भारत भ्रमण हो।

बैंकबाट लिएको ३४ करोड रुपैयाँ ऋण अपचलन गरेको आरोपमा बागमती प्रदेशका पूर्वमुख्यमन्त्री इन्द्र बानियाँविरुद्ध अदालतबाट प'क्राउ अनुमति लिइएको छ।

प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो (सीआईबी) ले बैंकिङ कसुरसम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउँदै गत साता नै अदालतबाट अनुमति लिएको हो। सीआईबीका अनुसार प्रभु बैंकबाट विभिन्न कम्पनीका नाममा लिइएको कर्जा निर्धारित उद्देश्यमा प्रयोग नभएको प्रारम्भिक अनुसन्धानबाट देखिएको छ।

नेपाल प्रिमियर लिग (एनपीएल) को तेस्रो सिजनमा चितवन राइनोजका बलर रिजन ढकाल सर्वोत्कृष्ट खेलाडी र उत्कृष्ट बलर घोषित भएका छन्।

दुवै विधामा उत्कृष्ट बनेका रिजनले सर्वोत्कृष्ट खेलाडी बनेबापत ओमोडाको कार र उत्कृष्ट बलर बनेबापत पल्सर बाइक प्राप्त गरेका छन्।

चितवनलाई प्लेअफ हुँदै दोस्रो क्वालिफायरसम्म पुर्‍याउन रिजनको बलिङ महत्त्वपूर्ण रह्यो। उनले प्रतियोगिताका ८ खेलमा १७ विकेट लिँदै सर्वाधिक विकेट लिने खेलाडी बने। बलिङतर्फ स्कट कुग्गेलिनले १० खेलमा १४ विकेट लिएका थिए।

यस्तै, विराटनगर किङ्सका लोकेश बम उत्कृष्ट ब्याटर घोषित भएका छन्। उनले यस उपलब्धिबापत पल्सर बाइक प्राप्त गरे। प्लेअफमा पुग्न नसकेको विराटनगरका लागि खेलेका लोकेशले ७ खेलमा २४२ रन बनाएका थिए।

पोखरा एभेन्जर्सका युवराज सामरा भने प्रतियोगिताका सर्वाधिक रनकर्ता बने। उनले ४ खेलमा २९४ रन जोडेका थिए। पोखरा पनि प्लेअफमा पुग्न सकेको थिएन।

नेपाल प्रिमियर लिग (एनपीएल) को छैटौँ संस्करणदेखि प्रतियोगिता होम एन्ड अवे प्रणालीमा सञ्चालन गर्ने तयारी गरिएको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहले लिगमा सहभागी आठवटै टोलीका लागि फ्लडलाइटयुक्त क्रिकेट रंगशाला निर्माण गर्ने घोषणा गरेका छन्।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाहका अनुसार सरकारले आठ टोलीलाई लक्षित गरी छुट्टाछुट्टै रंगशाला निर्माण गर्नेछ। यसका लागि नेपाल सरकारको पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्रालयले काम अघि बढाउनेछ।

फाप्ला क्रिकेट रंगशालाको निर्माण प्रक्रिया सुरु भइसकेको छ। बाँकी सात रंगशालाको निर्माण प्रक्रिया पनि आगामी तीन महिनाभित्र अघि बढाइने प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले बताएका छन्।

घोषित योजनाअनुसार विराटनगर किंग्सका लागि बैजनाथपुर, लुम्बिनी लायन्सका लागि सिद्धार्थ, कर्णाली याक्सका लागि सुर्खेत र सुदूरपश्चिम रोयल्सका लागि फाप्लामा रंगशाला निर्माण हुनेछ।

यसैगरी, काठमाडौं गुर्खाजका लागि कीर्तिपुर क्रिकेट मैदान, पोखरा एभेन्जर्सका लागि पोखरा क्रिकेट रंगशाला, जनकपुर बोल्ट्सका लागि रामजानकी क्रिकेट रंगशाला र चितवन राइनोजका लागि गौतमबुद्ध क्रिकेट रंगशाला बनाउने योजना छ।

नेपाली क्रिकेटको व्यावसायिक विकास र विस्तारका लागि आवश्यक पूर्वाधार निर्माण गर्न सरकार तयार रहेको प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भनाइ छ।

यसअघि सम्पन्न एनपीएल फाइनलमा सुदूरपश्चिम रोयल्सले लुम्बिनी लायन्सलाई १० विकेटले हराउँदै च्याम्पियन बनेको थियो।

आफूलाई ‘सञ्चारको सई’ बताउँदै छोरा हराएको जानकारी गराउन फोन गरेका सहकर्मीलाई गालीगलौज गर्ने जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय गौरमा कार्यरत प्रहरी हवल्दार बुधन महतोमाथि निलम्बन प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको छ। घटनासम्बन्धी अडियो सार्वजनिक भएपछि चौतर्फी आलोचना बढेसँगै रौतहट प्रहरीले उनीमाथि कारबाही प्रक्रिया सुरु गरेको हो।

मधेस प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालय जनकपुरधामले घटनाको सत्यतथ्य छानबिन गर्न निर्देशन दिएलगत्तै जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय रौतहटले हवल्दार महतो र पीडित प्रहरी हवल्दार सुरेश यादव दुवैलाई थप अनुसन्धानका लागि जनकपुर पठाएको छ।

जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय रौतहटका प्रमुख प्रहरी उपरीक्षक सिताराम रिजालले घटनाबारे अनुसन्धान भइरहेको जानकारी दिएका छन्। उनका अनुसार सार्वजनिक अडियोमा दुवै पक्षको गल्ती देखिएको छ। तर, हवल्दार महतोले आफूलाई प्रहरी सहायक निरीक्षक (सई) बताउँदै सहकर्मीमाथि गरेको गालीगलौजका विषयमा छुट्टै अनुसन्धान गरिनेछ।

छोराको खोजी तथा उद्धारका लागि सहयोग माग्न यादवले शुक्रबार जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालयको कन्ट्रोल रुममा सम्पर्क गरेका थिए। त्यहाँबाट सञ्चार शाखामा जानकारी गराउन भनिएपछि उनले उक्त शाखामा फोन गरेका थिए।

सार्वजनिक अडियोमा यादवले फोन उठाउने व्यक्तिसँग ‘को बोल्नुभयो सर, हवल्दारसाहेब कि असइसाहेब?’ भन्दै परिचय सोधेको सुनिन्छ। त्यसपछि आफूलाई सई बताउने महतोले ‘जय नेपाल’ नभनेको र बोल्ने शैली नमिलेको भन्दै यादवलाई झपारेका थिए। महतोले आफ्नो दर्जा बताउन नमिल्ने आशय व्यक्त गर्दै अपमानजनक शब्द प्रयोग गरी गालीगलौज गरेको पनि अडियोमा सुनिन्छ।

प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालयले घटनाको वास्तविकता पत्ता लगाई दोषी देखिएका प्रहरी कर्मचारीमाथि प्रहरी नियमावलीअनुसार आवश्यक कारबाही गर्न निर्देशन दिएको छ। सोही निर्देशनपछि रौतहट प्रहरीले हवल्दार महतोमाथि निलम्बन प्रक्रिया अघि बढाएको हो।

काठमाडौं । नेकपा एमालेका अध्यक्ष एवं पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओलीले राष्ट्रपति रामचन्द्र पौडेलमाथि कडा टिप्पणी गर्दै उनलाई ‘डरपोक’को संज्ञा दिएका छन्। उनले प्रतिनिधिसभा विघटन गर्ने निर्णय असंवैधानिक भएको दाबी गर्दै संसद् विघटन गरेर लोकतन्त्र जोगाउन नसकिने बताएका छन्।

शनिबार काठमाडौंमा नेकपा एमालेको जनवर्गीय संगठन नेशनल भोलेन्टियर फोर्सको प्रथम स्थापना दिवसका अवसरमा आयोजित कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै ओलीले वर्तमान सरकार गठनको प्रक्रिया नै असंवैधानिक र अलोकतान्त्रिक रहेको आरोप लगाए।

उनले अहिलेको सरकार बन्ने प्रक्रिया आतंक, आगजनी र तोडफोडबाट सुरु भएको टिप्पणी गर्दै संविधान र लोकतान्त्रिक विधि मिचेर सरकार गठन गरिएको दाबी गरे।

ओलीले पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीशसमेत रहेकी तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री सुशीला कार्कीको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न उठाउँदै प्रधानमन्त्री बनेपछि उनले असंवैधानिक रूपमा संसद् विघटनको सिफारिस गरेको आरोप लगाए।

राष्ट्रपति पौडेलको भूमिकामाथि कटाक्ष गर्दै ओलीले भने, ‘राष्ट्रपतिले डरपोक भएर प्रतिनिधिसभाको असंवैधानिक विघटन गर्नुभयो। बडो जुक्ति लगाएर लोकतन्त्र जोगाएँ भन्नुभयो। असंवैधानिक ढङ्गले संसद् विघटन गरेर लोकतन्त्र जोगिन्छ?’

उनले प्रधानमन्त्रीको कुर्सीमा कसले पुर्‍यायो भन्ने थाहा नपाइकन मनपरीतन्त्र चलाइएको आरोपसमेत लगाए। संविधान र लोकतान्त्रिक प्रक्रियाको पालना नगरी राज्य सञ्चालन गरिएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

त्यस्तै, प्रतिनिधिसभा विघटनविरुद्ध आफ्नो पार्टीले सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट निवेदन दायर गरे पनि अदालतले अहिलेसम्म फैसला नगरेको भन्दै ओलीले असन्तुष्टि व्यक्त गरे। अदालतले मुद्दामा आफ्नो पक्षमा वा विपक्षमा जे फैसला गरे पनि निर्णय दिनुपर्ने उनको भनाइ थियो।

‘हामीले असंवैधानिक ढङ्गले प्रतिनिधिसभा विघटन भयो भनेर मुद्दा हालेपछि ठिक छ, हराउनुस्, अन्याय गर्नुस्, तर फैसला त गर्नुस्। फैसला नगरी उहाँहरू चुप लागेर बस्नुभयो,’ ओलीले भने।

उनले लोकतन्त्र र संविधानको संरक्षण गर्ने जिम्मेवारी राज्यका निकायले पूरा नगरेको आरोप लगाउँदै लोकतान्त्रिक संस्थाहरू कमजोर पारिएको टिप्पणी गरे। राज्यका निकायहरू कुनै व्यक्तिको आदेशमा नभई संविधान र कानुनअनुसार सञ्चालन हुनुपर्नेमा पनि उनले जोड दिए।

देशलाई संवैधानिक तथा लोकतान्त्रिक विधिअनुसार सञ्चालन गर्न दबाब दिन युवाहरू संगठित हुनुपर्ने ओलीको भनाइ थियो।

प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाह ‘बालेन’ भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीको निमन्त्रणामा आइतबार भारत भ्रमणमा निस्कँदैछन्। दिउँसो १:४५ बजे काठमाडौंस्थित त्रिभुवन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलबाट दिल्ली प्रस्थान गर्ने उनको यो पहिलो औपचारिक विदेश भ्रमण हो।

दिल्लीको इन्दिरा गान्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलमा भारतीय वाणिज्य तथा उद्योग राज्यमन्त्री जितिन प्रसादले प्रधानमन्त्री शाहलाई स्वागत गर्ने कार्यक्रम छ। त्यसपछि उनले भारतीय विदेशमन्त्री एस जयशंकरसँग भेट गर्नेछन्।

मंसिर ७ गते राष्ट्रपति भवनमा औपचारिक स्वागत कार्यक्रम राखिएको छ। स्वागतपछि शाहले राजघाट पुगेर महात्मा गान्धीको समाधिस्थलमा श्रद्धाञ्जलि अर्पण गर्नेछन्। त्यसपछि हैदराबाद हाउसमा भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री मोदीसँग भेटवार्ता हुनेछ।

परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर राईका अनुसार दुई प्रधानमन्त्रीबीच सुरुमा व्यक्तिगत र त्यसपछि दुवै देशका प्रतिनिधिमण्डलको सहभागितामा छलफल हुनेछ। भेटवार्तापछि संयुक्त पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्ने तथा दुई देशबीचका समझदारी र सम्झौतापत्र आदानप्रदान गर्ने तयारी छ।

भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भारतीय राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मूसँग पनि शिष्टाचार भेट गर्नेछन्।

नेपाल–भारत व्यापारिक बैठकमा भारतीय मन्त्रीको उपस्थिति शून्य!

प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाहको भारतको राजकीय भ्रमणका क्रममा नोभेम्बर २२ मा नयाँ दिल्लीमा आयोजना हुने भारत–नेपाल व्यापारिक बैठकमा कुनै पनि भारतीय मन्त्री सहभागी नहुने भएका छन्। नेपालले भारतबाट थप लगानी भित्र्याउने र आर्थिक सम्बन्ध विस्तार गर्ने लक्ष्यसहित यो बैठकलाई महत्त्वपूर्ण रूपमा लिएको समयमा भारतीय मन्त्रीको अनुपस्थितिलाई चासोका साथ हेरिएको छ।

नेपालको आर्थिक विकासका प्राथमिकतामा सहयोग जुटाउने र दुई देशबीचको लगानी तथा व्यापारिक सम्बन्धलाई थप मजबुत बनाउने उद्देश्यले बैठक आयोजना गर्न लागिएको हो। तर, भारतीय मन्त्रीस्तरीय प्रतिनिधित्व नहुने भएपछि लगानीसम्बन्धी छलफलमा राजनीतिक तहको सहभागिता कस्तो रहने भन्ने प्रश्नसमेत उठेको छ।

नयाँ दिल्लीस्थित ताजमहल होटलमा आयोजना हुने उक्त बैठकको संयुक्त आयोजना भारतीय उद्योग परिसंघ (सीआईआई) र नेपाल उद्योग वाणिज्य महासंघ (एफएनसीसीआई) ले गर्दैछन्। बैठकमा नेपालका अर्थमन्त्री स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले मुख्य मन्तव्य दिनेछन् भने परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले विशेष सम्बोधन गर्ने कार्यक्रम छ।

त्यस्तै, भारतीय उद्योग परिसंघका अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय परिषद्का सहअध्यक्ष तथा सन इन्टरनेसनल लिमिटेडका अध्यक्ष विक्रमजित सिंह साहनी, नेपाल उद्योग वाणिज्य महासंघका अध्यक्ष अञ्जन श्रेष्ठ, महासंघकी पूर्वअध्यक्ष तथा भारत–नेपाल संयुक्त व्यापार मञ्चकी सहअध्यक्ष भवानी राणा र लगानी बोर्ड नेपालकी प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत याङ्की उक्याबले पनि कार्यक्रममा धारणा राख्नेछन्।

दुवै देशका उद्योगी तथा व्यवसायी प्रतिनिधिहरूले व्यापार, लगानी र आर्थिक सहकार्यका विषयमा आफ्ना धारणा राख्ने कार्यक्रम रहेको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा छिमेकी मुलुकबाट थप लगानी आकर्षित गर्ने प्रयास गरिरहेका बेला व्यापारिक बैठकमा भारतीय मन्त्रीको अनुपस्थितिले भ्रमणको आर्थिक एजेन्डाबारे थप चासो बढाएको छ।

छोरा बेपत्ता भएको जानकारी गराउन फोन गरेका सहकर्मीलाई गालीगलौज गर्ने रौतहट जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालयका हवल्दार बुधन महतोमाथि निलम्बन प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको छ। घटनाको अडियो सार्वजनिक भएपछि चौतर्फी आलोचना बढेसँगै मधेश प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालयको निर्देशनमा रौतहट प्रहरीले छानबिन सुरु गरेको हो।

घटनाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न हवल्दार महतो र पीडित हवल्दार सुरेश यादवलाई जनकपुर पठाइएको छ। रौतहट प्रहरी प्रमुख एसपी सिताराम रिजालले दुवै पक्षको भूमिकाबारे अनुसन्धान भइरहेको बताएका छन्।

यादवका १७ वर्षीय छोरा चन्दनकुमार दुई दिनअघि घरबाट बेपत्ता भएका थिए। उनको खोजीका लागि शुक्रबार जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालयको कन्ट्रोल रुममा सम्पर्क गरेका यादवलाई सञ्चार शाखामा फोन गर्न भनिएको थियो। त्यसपछि सञ्चार शाखामा फोन गर्दा महतोले आफूलाई सइ बताउँदै ‘जय नेपाल’ नगरेको र बोल्ने शैली नमिलेको भन्दै गालीगलौज गरेको अडियोमा सुनिन्छ।

प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालयका प्रवक्ता एसएसपी प्रभुप्रसाद ढकालले विज्ञप्ति जारी गर्दै प्रहरी कर्मचारीबीचको संवादमा प्रयोग भएको भाषा, शब्द र शैलीप्रति गम्भीर ध्यानाकर्षण भएको जनाएका छन्।

गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले राजनीतिक दलको पक्षमा काम गर्ने र नेताको चाकडीमा लाग्ने राष्ट्रसेवक कर्मचारीमाथि कानुनअनुसार कडा कारबाही गर्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन्। शनिबार सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत उनले कर्मचारीलाई आफ्नो पदीय जिम्मेवारी र कर्तव्य नबिर्सन सचेत गराएका हुन्।

सरकार गठन भएदेखि नै कर्मचारीको मुख्य जिम्मेवारी देश र जनताको सेवा गर्नु रहेको स्पष्ट पार्दै आएको उल्लेख गरेका गुरुङले राजनीतिक गतिविधिमा संलग्न हुने भ्रम त्याग्न आग्रह गरेका छन्। जनताको कामभन्दा नेताको चाकडीलाई प्राथमिकता दिने कर्मचारीलाई कुनै छुट नदिइने उनको भनाइ छ।

सरकारलाई नेताको चाकडी गर्ने नभई जनताको दुःख बुझ्ने, आफ्नो कर्तव्य पूरा गर्ने र देशप्रति इमानदार राष्ट्रसेवक आवश्यक रहेको उनले बताएका छन्।

इंग्ल्यान्डका स्टार फुटबलर ह्यारी केन चोटका कारण केही महिना फुटबल खेल्न नसक्ने अवस्थामा!

इंग्ल्यान्डका कप्तान तथा बायर्न म्युनिखका स्टार स्ट्राइकर ह्यारी केन चोटका कारण केही महिना फुटबल मैदानबाट बाहिर रहने भएका छन्।

शुक्रबार जर्मन बुन्डेसलिगाअन्तर्गत कोलोनविरुद्धको खेलमा केनको बायाँ गोलीगाँठोको लिगामेन्टमा चोट लागेको हो। चोटपछि उनी खेलको २० औँ मिनेटमै मैदानबाट बाहिरिएका थिए।

Hypocrisy of Neighbour: India Trades Billions With China but Blocks Nepal's Electricity Over Chinese Walkie-Talkies

India maintains a massive trade relationship with China, yet Nepal's 42 MW hydropower project reportedly cannot sell electricity to the Indian market because Chinese-made walkie-talkies were used during construction.

India's approach to Chinese involvement in Nepal's hydropower sector has raised questions about its electricity import policy, particularly as the country continues to maintain billions of dollars in trade with China.

In a striking example, India has reportedly refused to purchase electricity generated by Nepal's 42 MW Mystery Khola Hydropower Project in Myagdi, despite the project being developed with entirely domestic investment. According to senior officials at Nepal's Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, the project faced difficulties securing Indian approval because Chinese-made walkie-talkies were used during construction.

The walkie-talkies were reportedly used by technical personnel for communication while building the project. However, their use allegedly became an obstacle to exporting the electricity to India.

The case has raised questions about whether India's restrictions on Chinese-linked projects are being applied consistently.

Billions in Trade With China, But Restrictions on Nepal

India continues to conduct extensive trade with China, despite longstanding political and security tensions between the two countries.

According to trade figures for the 2024–25 financial year, India-China bilateral merchandise trade reached approximately $127.7 billion, with Indian imports from China accounting for around $113.46 billion.

China remains one of India's largest trading partners, supplying a wide range of goods, including electronics, machinery, industrial equipment and manufacturing components.

Yet, when it comes to electricity imports from Nepal, India's policy takes a restrictive approach towards projects involving Chinese investment, ownership or influence.

The Mystery Khola case is particularly striking because, according to Nepalese energy officials, the project was built using domestic investment, with Chinese involvement reportedly limited to communication equipment used during construction.

India's Restrictions Affect Nepal's Hydropower Industry

India's electricity import policy considers the source of investment, beneficial ownership and effective control of hydropower projects in neighbouring countries.

Clause 6.3 of the Central Electricity Authority's procedure for approving and facilitating cross-border electricity trade, issued on February 26, 2021, contains provisions concerning investment and ownership linked to neighbouring countries.

These restrictions have created challenges for Nepali hydropower developers seeking to export electricity to India, particularly those involving Chinese investors or companies.

The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission's 2019 Cross Border Trade of Electricity Regulations establish the broader framework for electricity trading between India and neighbouring countries. However, the specific restrictions concerning Chinese investment and ownership are contained in the separate 2021 procedure.

As a result, some Nepali energy producers have reportedly reconsidered Chinese investment because of concerns that electricity generated by such projects may not receive permission to enter the Indian market.

Some developers have even abandoned plans involving Chinese investors and sought alternative investment sources.

India Allows Chinese Companies to Bid for Projects Within Its Own Borders

Adding another dimension to the issue, India has also taken steps to ease restrictions on certain Chinese-linked companies operating within its own electricity sector.

According to the report, four Chinese-linked electricity equipment manufacturers operating production facilities in India were allowed to participate in government tenders for sensitive power projects.

The companies include:

TBEA Energy

Nanjing Electric India

New Northeast Electric India

Taikai Electric (India)

India's Finance Ministry reportedly issued an order in June allowing these companies to participate in government procurement processes. Earlier, in January, the Ministry of Power had requested the Finance Ministry to consider relaxing restrictions for Chinese companies manufacturing equipment within India.

This creates an apparent contrast: Chinese-linked manufacturers can compete for certain electricity-sector contracts within India, while Nepal faces restrictions on exporting electricity from projects involving Chinese investment or equipment.

Nepal to Raise the Issue During Prime Minister Balendra Shah's India Visit

Nepal is preparing to raise the issue during Prime Minister Balendra Shah's upcoming state visit to India.

The government plans to request greater flexibility in India's electricity import policy and seek easier access to the Indian energy market for Nepali hydropower projects involving Chinese investment, companies or equipment.

Nepal also wants India to adopt a more accommodating approach towards electricity generated by projects that have already been completed or are currently under construction.

Former Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal had previously told a parliamentary committee that India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar had expressed reservations about purchasing electricity from hydropower projects directly invested in by China in Nepal.

The issue therefore extends beyond a single hydropower project and has become an important concern for Nepal's energy investment and export ambitions.

Nepal Currently Exports 56 MW of Electricity to India

Despite the challenges, Nepal has received approval to export electricity generated by three hydropower projects to India's Indian Energy Exchange (IEX).

The Nepal Electricity Authority has been authorised to sell a combined 56 MW of electricity from Mangsir 1 until Shrawan 15, 2084, according to the report.

However, restrictions affecting Chinese-linked hydropower projects continue to create uncertainty for Nepal's plans to expand electricity exports.

A Question of Consistency in India's China Policy

India's extensive trade with China, combined with its restrictions on electricity imports from Chinese-linked hydropower projects in Nepal, has brought its cross-border energy policy under scrutiny.

While India continues to import billions of dollars' worth of Chinese goods and permits certain Chinese-linked manufacturers to participate in domestic power-sector tenders, Nepalese hydropower developers face barriers when attempting to sell electricity to the Indian market.

The Mystery Khola project highlights the issue in an unusual way: a hydropower project developed with Nepali investment reportedly encountered difficulties over walkie-talkies used by construction personnel.

As Nepal seeks to expand its electricity exports and attract international investment, the question remains whether India will adopt a more flexible and consistent approach towards Nepal's hydropower sector.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah's upcoming visit could provide an opportunity for Nepal to seek clarification and push for changes to the existing restrictions.

धानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहको दुईदिने भारतको राजकीय भ्रमणलाई भारत सरकारले पनि औपचारिक रूपमा घोषणा गरेको छ। भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीको निमन्त्रणामा प्रधानमन्त्री शाह मंसिर ६ र ७ गते भारत भ्रमणमा जाने भएका हुन्।

भारतको विदेश मन्त्रालयले शुक्रबार जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भ्रमण मिति सार्वजनिक गर्दै प्रधानमन्त्री बनेपछि उनी पहिलोपटक भारत भ्रमणमा आउन लागेको जनाएको छ।

भ्रमणका क्रममा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भारतीय राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मुसँग शिष्टाचार भेट गर्ने कार्यक्रम छ। त्यस्तै, मंसिर ७ गते भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीसँग द्विपक्षीय भेटवार्ता हुनेछ।

भारतीय विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार उक्त वार्तामा नेपाल–भारत सम्बन्धका समग्र पक्षको समीक्षा गरिनेछ। साथै, आपसी हितसँग सम्बन्धित क्षेत्रीय तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विषयमा पनि छलफल हुनेछ।

भारतले नेपालसँगको सम्बन्धलाई आफ्नो ‘छिमेक पहिलो’ नीतिअन्तर्गत विशेष महत्त्व दिँदै आएको विज्ञप्तिमा उल्लेख गरेको छ। दुवै देशबीच ऐतिहासिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा जनस्तरमा घनिष्ठ सम्बन्ध रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै भारतले व्यापार, विकास साझेदारी, ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत तथा भौतिक र डिजिटल सम्पर्क सञ्जालका क्षेत्रमा सहकार्य विस्तार भइरहेको जनाएको छ।

त्यसैगरी, स्टार्टअप, प्रविधि, नवप्रवर्तन र खेलकुदजस्ता नयाँ क्षेत्रमा पनि दुई देशबीच सहकार्य बढिरहेको भारतको भनाइ छ।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भ्रमणलाई दुई देशबीच हुँदै आएको उच्चस्तरीय नियमित आदानप्रदानको निरन्तरताका रूपमा व्याख्या गर्दै भारतीय विदेश मन्त्रालयले यसले द्विपक्षीय साझेदारी थप सुदृढ बनाउन सहयोग पुग्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेको छ।

यसअघि नेपालको परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयले पनि प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको भारत भ्रमणको औपचारिक कार्यतालिका सार्वजनिक गरिसकेको थियो। शुक्रबार बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले समेत भ्रमणलाई स्वीकृति दिएको छ।

भ्रमणका क्रममा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री मोदीसँग प्रतिनिधिमण्डलस्तरीय वार्ता गर्ने, राष्ट्रपति मुर्मुसँग भेटघाट गर्ने तथा विभिन्न समझदारीपत्रमा हस्ताक्षर र परियोजनाहरूको उद्घाटन गर्ने कार्यक्रम रहेको छ।
झन्डै दुई वर्षदेखि प्रसारण रोकिएको लोकप्रिय हास्य सिरियल 'सक्किगोनि' नयाँ सिजनसहित दर्शकमाझ फर्किने भएको छ।

बालेन काठमाडौंको मेयर हुँदा राष्ट्रपति कार्यालय, सिंहदरबार लगायत प्रमुख स्थानको फोहोर उठेन। 

त्यसमा परेको मुद्दामा अन्तिम फैसलाको पूर्णपाठ हालै तयार भई सार्वजनिक भएको छ।  

त्यसमा सर्वोच्चले तत्कालीन मेयर शाहको फोहोर नउठाउने निर्णयबाट नागरिकका संवैधानिक मौलिक हक उल्लंघन भएको व्याख्या गरेको छ।

के छ पूर्णपाठमा?

कोप–३१ को निर्णय मस्यौदा नेपालका लागि कत्तिको उपलब्धिमूलक छ? हिमालसम्बन्धी प्रस्ताव अन्तिम निर्णयमा जोगाउन के गर्नुपर्छ? अनि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय जलवायु वार्ताका उपलब्धि प्रभावित नागरिकको जीवनसम्म किन पुगिरहेका छैनन्?

AFTER MORE THAN A MONTH TRAPPED IN A CITY CANAL, BUKANGI FINALLY HEADED TOWARD THE OPEN SEA. 🦈🌊

A female dusky shark nicknamed Bukangi became an unexpected sensation in Busan, South Korea, after she was first spotted swimming in an artificial canal on September 18, 2026.

The approximately 3-meter-long shark attracted more than 1.6 million visitors, with people gathering along the waterfront to watch her and hope for her safe return to the ocean.

After two unsuccessful rescue attempts, authorities launched a third operation on October 21. Using floating platforms, nets, and divers, the rescue team carefully guided Bukangi along the canal toward the sea.

After 33 days in the waterway, she finally swam out toward open waters. However, she later returned near the canal entrance, and officials continued monitoring her movements.

Bukangi's story captured the hearts of many and reminded people that even a powerful ocean predator can become vulnerable when trapped in an environment it cannot easily escape.

A HEARTBREAKING SCENE UNFOLDS ON NEW ZEALAND'S COASTLINE. 💔🐋

On November 19, 2026, approximately 24 sperm whales became stranded at Ninety Mile Beach (Te Oneroa a Tōhe) in New Zealand's Far North.

The local Māori iwi, Te Aupōuri, confirmed the stranding and announced that a customary process was underway. Public access was restricted between The Bluff and Scotts Point while the situation was being managed.

Sadly, a subsequent update from New Zealand's Department of Conservation reported that 19 whales had died, while five others remained alive but in poor health.

The cause of the mass stranding has not yet been confirmed. Sperm whales are deep-diving marine mammals that live in complex social groups, making mass strandings particularly distressing.

This tragic incident is another reminder of how vulnerable marine mammals can be when they become stranded.

A LIFE LOST AFTER WASHING ASHORE ON NEW ZEALAND'S COAST. 💔🐋

A pilot whale has died shortly after becoming stranded on Pukehina Beach in New Zealand's Bay of Plenty on November 18, 2026.

According to reports, members of the public discovered the whale alive on the beach and alerted authorities. However, despite being alive when first found, the animal died shortly afterward.

Project Jonah community lead Louisa Hawkes confirmed the incident, while New Zealand's Department of Conservation was also responding to the situation.

Pilot whales are highly social marine mammals that live in close-knit family groups. Strandings can occur for several reasons, including illness, injury, disorientation, or social behavior within a pod. The exact reason for this whale's stranding has not been established.

Every stranding is a heartbreaking reminder of the challenges these ocean mammals face.

“THE FIRST RULE OF SURVIVING AN AMBUSH: FIGHT THROUGH THE INITIAL SHOCK.” — When three MS-13 gang members opened fire point-blank into her patrol car window at 3:30 AM, Officer Ann Carrizales didn't collapse or curl into a defensive posture. Her Marine Corps muscle memory took over: bleeding from the cheek and chest, she returned fire through her windshield and initiated a 20-mile pursuit at 100 mph.

“When that round hit my face, it felt like being struck with a baseball bat. But in the Marine Corps, you're conditioned to push past the shock and stay in the fight. Giving up was never an option. My only thought was: You picked the wrong cop, and you're not getting away with this.”

 Officer Ann Carrizales, Former USMC Military Police & Stafford Police Department

 Ambush statistics show that most fatal encounters occur within the first three seconds when victims freeze or attempt to retreat without returning fire. Carrizales absorbed rounds to both her face and Kevlar chest vest, immediately clearing leather and returning lethal fire into the threat vehicle to disrupt the shooters' momentum.

Recognizing that transitioning out of the patrol unit in the kill zone would leave her exposed, she engaged the suspects directly through her cruiser glass, suppressing the vehicle before they could deliver follow-up headshots.

 Despite significant blood loss and acoustic trauma from enclosed gunfire, she broadcasted suspect descriptions, vehicle coordinates, and direction of travel across regional dispatch channels, driving over 100 mph from Stafford into Houston until the suspects crashed out and were taken into custody.

 Prior to joining the Stafford Police Department, Carrizales served as a Military Police officer and competed as a champion boxer in the Marine Corps, building the neurological resilience and stress-inoculation required to execute dynamic tactical decisions while severely wounded.

“14 DIRECT HITS WITH .45 ACP. SIX MORTAL ORGAN WOUNDS. AND HE WAS STILL FIRING.” — The harrowing 2008 Illinois shootout that permanently changed modern police loadouts, proving why handguns are marginal stoppers and why Officer Tim Gramins never goes on patrol with fewer than 145 rounds.

“People ask me all the time, ‘Why do you carry so much ammunition? Are you paranoid?’ I tell them: It’s not paranoia. It’s preparation. I’ve been down to my last four bullets in a gunfight with a man who absorbed six fatal hits and kept trying to kill me. I will never let that happen again.”

 Officer Tim Gramins, Skokie Police Department Firearms Instructor

Tactical Breakdown: The 56-Second Gunfight
The Immediate Ambush: On a quiet August afternoon in Skokie, Illinois, Officer Tim Gramins initiated a traffic stop on a bank robbery suspect. Before Gramins could unbuckle his seatbelt, the suspect stepped out and immediately opened fire at close range, dumping rounds through Gramins' cruiser windshield.

 Gramins fired 33 rounds of heavy .45 ACP from his Glock 21, scoring 14 direct torso hits. Despite suffering six non-survivable wounds—including damage to his heart, both lungs, liver, diaphragm, and kidney—the suspect continued maneuvering, reloading, and firing for nearly a minute on sheer adrenaline and rage.

Burning through his primary magazine and two belt reloads, Gramins found himself pinned down behind the suspect's vehicle with only four rounds remaining in his entire arsenal. Recognizing that center-mass hits were not stopping the threat, he took deliberate aim under incoming fire and delivered three headshots to finally neutralize the gunman.

 Prior to the incident, Gramins carried a standard patrol loadout of 47 rounds. Realizing that a second suspect would have left him with an empty gun, Gramins transitioned his carry setup to 145 rounds of 9mm—carrying three 17-round spare magazines on his duty belt, two 33-round extended magazines in his active-shooter plate carrier, and a backup firearm.

 Handgun calibers (.45 ACP, .40 S&W, 9mm) do not create catastrophic hydrostatic shock like rifle rounds. Unless a round disrupts the brainstem or upper cervical spine, a determined adversary can remain functional for 30 to 60 seconds even with zero blood pressure.

 High-speed, dynamic gunfights burn through ammunition at roughly 3 to 4 rounds per second. When movement, vehicle cover, and adrenaline degrade precision, capacity is often the difference between winning and running dry.

When multiple center-mass hits fail to alter an attacker's behavior within seconds, officers must immediately recognize the failure to stop and transition to cranial or pelvic vault targets.

US Marines have wrapped up their latest rotation in Australia, and it was a first on more than one count.

Over about seven months, roughly 2,000 Marines of Marine Rotational Force-Darwin trained in Australia's Northern Territory and across five Pacific nations, New Caledonia, French Polynesia, the Philippines and Papua New Guinea. For the first time, the force brought first-person-view (FPV) attack drones, 10 Neros Archers, along with a Tactical Resupply Unmanned Aircraft System that in July flew a refrigerated container of simulated blood between two aid stations in Queensland.

"You watch what is happening in Ukraine," said Col. George Flynn, the force commander, pointing to how heavily drones now feature in modern fighting. He said every military is looking for more ways both to use drones and to defend against them, while stressing that Marines still have to be able to operate in austere, challenging conditions.

US Marines have rotated through northern Australia each year since 2012. This was the first rotation certified as a Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force, a crisis-response designation. The last Marines returned to Camp Pendleton, California, in late October.

November 21, 2010.
Marjah, Afghanistan.

Cpl. Kyle Carpenter and Lance Cpl. Nick Eufrazio were on a rooftop when an enemy grenade landed between them.

“When you look through the glass at 3,540 meters, you aren’t just looking down a street—you’re looking across entire cities. You’re factoring in the curvature of the earth, the temperature of the air, the mirage, crosswinds between multiple mountain corridors, and Coriolis effect.

We spotted the target on a rooftop engaging coalition forces. The range was so extreme that nobody had ever even attempted an engagement at that distance in combat history.

Squeeze the trigger. Boom.

The bullet left the chamber, and then you wait. At that distance, the round doesn’t hit instantly. It flew for nearly ten full seconds. You have enough time to breathe, blink, reset your sight picture, and have a brief conversation with your spotter while the bullet is traveling across the sky.

Ten seconds later: Impact. Target drops instantly.

When the confirmation came through, we didn’t celebrate. You just look at each other in absolute disbelief that physics allowed that to happen.”

Firing a .50 BMG McMillan TAC-50 from a high-rise rooftop during the 2017 siege of Mosul, Alexander and his spotter smashed the previous world record by more than 1,000 meters—saving dozens of allied troops pinned down below.

“THE FIRST RULE OF SURVIVING AN AMBUSH: FIGHT THROUGH THE INITIAL SHOCK.” — When three MS-13 gang members opened fire point-blank into her patrol car window at 3:30 AM, Officer Ann Carrizales didn't collapse or curl into a defensive posture. Her Marine Corps muscle memory took over: bleeding from the cheek and chest, she returned fire through her windshield and initiated a 20-mile pursuit at 100 mph.

“When that round hit my face, it felt like being struck with a baseball bat. But in the Marine Corps, you're conditioned to push past the shock and stay in the fight. Giving up was never an option. My only thought was: You picked the wrong cop, and you're not getting away with this.”

 Officer Ann Carrizales, Former USMC Military Police & Stafford Police Department

 Ambush statistics show that most fatal encounters occur within the first three seconds when victims freeze or attempt to retreat without returning fire. Carrizales absorbed rounds to both her face and Kevlar chest vest, immediately clearing leather and returning lethal fire into the threat vehicle to disrupt the shooters' momentum.

Recognizing that transitioning out of the patrol unit in the kill zone would leave her exposed, she engaged the suspects directly through her cruiser glass, suppressing the vehicle before they could deliver follow-up headshots.

 Despite significant blood loss and acoustic trauma from enclosed gunfire, she broadcasted suspect descriptions, vehicle coordinates, and direction of travel across regional dispatch channels, driving over 100 mph from Stafford into Houston until the suspects crashed out and were taken into custody.

 Prior to joining the Stafford Police Department, Carrizales served as a Military Police officer and competed as a champion boxer in the Marine Corps, building the neurological resilience and stress-inoculation required to execute dynamic tactical decisions while severely wounded.

“14 DIRECT HITS WITH .45 ACP. SIX MORTAL ORGAN WOUNDS. AND HE WAS STILL FIRING.” — The harrowing 2008 Illinois shootout that permanently changed modern police loadouts, proving why handguns are marginal stoppers and why Officer Tim Gramins never goes on patrol with fewer than 145 rounds.

“People ask me all the time, ‘Why do you carry so much ammunition? Are you paranoid?’ I tell them: It’s not paranoia. It’s preparation. I’ve been down to my last four bullets in a gunfight with a man who absorbed six fatal hits and kept trying to kill me. I will never let that happen again.”

 Officer Tim Gramins, Skokie Police Department Firearms Instructor

Tactical Breakdown: The 56-Second Gunfight
The Immediate Ambush: On a quiet August afternoon in Skokie, Illinois, Officer Tim Gramins initiated a traffic stop on a bank robbery suspect. Before Gramins could unbuckle his seatbelt, the suspect stepped out and immediately opened fire at close range, dumping rounds through Gramins' cruiser windshield.

 Gramins fired 33 rounds of heavy .45 ACP from his Glock 21, scoring 14 direct torso hits. Despite suffering six non-survivable wounds—including damage to his heart, both lungs, liver, diaphragm, and kidney—the suspect continued maneuvering, reloading, and firing for nearly a minute on sheer adrenaline and rage.

Burning through his primary magazine and two belt reloads, Gramins found himself pinned down behind the suspect's vehicle with only four rounds remaining in his entire arsenal. Recognizing that center-mass hits were not stopping the threat, he took deliberate aim under incoming fire and delivered three headshots to finally neutralize the gunman.

 Prior to the incident, Gramins carried a standard patrol loadout of 47 rounds. Realizing that a second suspect would have left him with an empty gun, Gramins transitioned his carry setup to 145 rounds of 9mm—carrying three 17-round spare magazines on his duty belt, two 33-round extended magazines in his active-shooter plate carrier, and a backup firearm.

 Handgun calibers (.45 ACP, .40 S&W, 9mm) do not create catastrophic hydrostatic shock like rifle rounds. Unless a round disrupts the brainstem or upper cervical spine, a determined adversary can remain functional for 30 to 60 seconds even with zero blood pressure.

 High-speed, dynamic gunfights burn through ammunition at roughly 3 to 4 rounds per second. When movement, vehicle cover, and adrenaline degrade precision, capacity is often the difference between winning and running dry.

When multiple center-mass hits fail to alter an attacker's behavior within seconds, officers must immediately recognize the failure to stop and transition to cranial or pelvic vault targets.

— Detective Jared Reston, Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office & Medal of Valor Recipient

Tactical Breakdown: Surviving 7 Point-Blank Rounds

Troopers of the Rhodesian Light Infantry, known to the Rhodesian press as the "troopies." The RLI was formed on February 1, 1961, at Brady Barracks in Bulawayo as a light infantry battalion of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, recruiting only white soldiers. After the federation broke up, it became part of the Rhodesian Army, and in 1964 it was reorganized into a commando battalion, the role it would hold for the rest of its existence.

The battalion's famous nickname came from the men themselves. When the troopers chose "The Saints," their first commanding officer, Lt. Col. John Salt, approved it, and "When the Saints Go Marching In" became the regimental march. The battalion even received a pair of cheetah cubs as mascots. In the field, practicality won over regulation, and troopers on operations typically wore light T-shirts and shorts.

From 1974, the RLI ran an overseas recruitment program, drawing volunteers from Britain, South Africa, the United States, Australia, and beyond, many of them veterans of other wars. Its largest intake ever came in May 1976. After the war ended, the battalion briefly served under the new government of Zimbabwe before laying up its colours on October 17, 1980, and disbanding two weeks later.

In one of the most iconic long-range ballistics breakdowns in the history of The Shawn Ryan Show (Episodes #047 & #050), former Canadian Tier 1 Joint Task Force 2 (JTF2) sniper Dallas Alexander detailed the world-record combat kill in Mosul, Iraq—engaging an ISIS machine-gun crew from over 2.2 miles away.

In his own words:

“When you look through the glass at 3,540 meters, you aren’t just looking down a street—you’re looking across entire cities. You’re factoring in the curvature of the earth, the temperature of the air, the mirage, crosswinds between multiple mountain corridors, and Coriolis effect.

We spotted the target on a rooftop engaging coalition forces. The range was so extreme that nobody had ever even attempted an engagement at that distance in combat history.

My spotter did the calculations. We dialed the elevation so high that the barrel was literally pointing into the sky above the skyline.

Squeeze the trigger. Boom.

The bullet left the chamber, and then you wait. At that distance, the round doesn’t hit instantly. It flew for nearly ten full seconds. You have enough time to breathe, blink, reset your sight picture, and have a brief conversation with your spotter while the bullet is traveling across the sky.

Ten seconds later: Impact. Target drops instantly.

When the confirmation came through, we didn’t celebrate. You just look at each other in absolute disbelief that physics allowed that to happen.”

Firing a .50 BMG McMillan TAC-50 from a high-rise rooftop during the 2017 siege of Mosul, Alexander and his spotter smashed the previous world record by more than 1,000 meters—saving dozens of allied troops pinned down below.

Waiting ten full seconds for a bullet to cross the sky and strike an enemy position over two miles away pushes the boundaries of human precision and physics.

“14 DIRECT HITS WITH .45 ACP. SIX MORTAL ORGAN WOUNDS. AND HE WAS STILL FIRING.” — The harrowing 2008 Illinois shootout that permanently changed modern police loadouts, proving why handguns are marginal stoppers and why Officer Tim Gramins never goes on patrol with fewer than 145 rounds.

“People ask me all the time, ‘Why do you carry so much ammunition? Are you paranoid?’ I tell them: It’s not paranoia. It’s preparation. I’ve been down to my last four bullets in a gunfight with a man who absorbed six fatal hits and kept trying to kill me. I will never let that happen again.”

 Officer Tim Gramins, Skokie Police Department Firearms Instructor

Tactical Breakdown: The 56-Second Gunfight
The Immediate Ambush: On a quiet August afternoon in Skokie, Illinois, Officer Tim Gramins initiated a traffic stop on a bank robbery suspect. Before Gramins could unbuckle his seatbelt, the suspect stepped out and immediately opened fire at close range, dumping rounds through Gramins' cruiser windshield.

 Gramins fired 33 rounds of heavy .45 ACP from his Glock 21, scoring 14 direct torso hits. Despite suffering six non-survivable wounds—including damage to his heart, both lungs, liver, diaphragm, and kidney—the suspect continued maneuvering, reloading, and firing for nearly a minute on sheer adrenaline and rage.

Burning through his primary magazine and two belt reloads, Gramins found himself pinned down behind the suspect's vehicle with only four rounds remaining in his entire arsenal. Recognizing that center-mass hits were not stopping the threat, he took deliberate aim under incoming fire and delivered three headshots to finally neutralize the gunman.

 Prior to the incident, Gramins carried a standard patrol loadout of 47 rounds. Realizing that a second suspect would have left him with an empty gun, Gramins transitioned his carry setup to 145 rounds of 9mm—carrying three 17-round spare magazines on his duty belt, two 33-round extended magazines in his active-shooter plate carrier, and a backup firearm.

 Handgun calibers (.45 ACP, .40 S&W, 9mm) do not create catastrophic hydrostatic shock like rifle rounds. Unless a round disrupts the brainstem or upper cervical spine, a determined adversary can remain functional for 30 to 60 seconds even with zero blood pressure.

 High-speed, dynamic gunfights burn through ammunition at roughly 3 to 4 rounds per second. When movement, vehicle cover, and adrenaline degrade precision, capacity is often the difference between winning and running dry.

When multiple center-mass hits fail to alter an attacker's behavior within seconds, officers must immediately recognize the failure to stop and transition to cranial or pelvic vault targets.

“I remember looking over and seeing Jay [Jason Redman]. I remember him sitting upright, and I watched him get shot one more time, right in the face. He hit the ground so hard you knew he was dead.

We’re stuck behind a tractor tire that’s halfway out of the ground, serving no purpose, taking fire from every angle. It’s pitch black.

The bravest thing I have ever seen in 17 years happened on that night.

I watched Maddie get up and run forward after he had already been shot. He grabs our corpsman and starts dragging him backwards. Just like in the movies, the corpsman pulls his pistol, shooting into the woodline.

Maddie gets shot again—it spins him around and dumps him. He gets back up, grabs him, and gets shot again. Dumps him, gets back up, and continues dragging him until we got them all behind that tire.

Jason took one to the face that basically removed his jaw, removed his nose, and you could look inside him. Maddie’s arm was completely shattered. We basically just dog-piled on top of them. Plates on plates, just trying to build up a human wall so our brothers wouldn't take another bullet.”

Against all medical odds, Jason Redman survived the devastating facial gunshot wound, enduring dozens of reconstructive surgeries and going on to inspire millions across the veteran community.

Getting shot, knocked to the dirt, getting back up under machine-gun fire, and continuing to drag your wounded brothers to cover is the purest embodiment of brotherhood under fire.

“3,540 METERS. THE BULLET WAS IN THE AIR FOR ALMOST TEN SECONDS BEFORE IMPACT.” — JTF2 Sniper Dallas Alexander on The Shawn Ryan Show.

In one of the most iconic long-range ballistics breakdowns in the history of The Shawn Ryan Show (Episodes #047 & #050), former Canadian Tier 1 Joint Task Force 2 (JTF2) sniper Dallas Alexander detailed the world-record combat kill in Mosul, Iraq—engaging an ISIS machine-gun crew from over 2.2 miles away.

In his own words:

“When you look through the glass at 3,540 meters, you aren’t just looking down a street—you’re looking across entire cities. You’re factoring in the curvature of the earth, the temperature of the air, the mirage, crosswinds between multiple mountain corridors, and Coriolis effect.

We spotted the target on a rooftop engaging coalition forces. The range was so extreme that nobody had ever even attempted an engagement at that distance in combat history.

My spotter did the calculations. We dialed the elevation so high that the barrel was literally pointing into the sky above the skyline.

Squeeze the trigger. Boom.

The bullet left the chamber, and then you wait. At that distance, the round doesn’t hit instantly. It flew for nearly ten full seconds. You have enough time to breathe, blink, reset your sight picture, and have a brief conversation with your spotter while the bullet is traveling across the sky.

Ten seconds later: Impact. Target drops instantly.

When the confirmation came through, we didn’t celebrate. You just look at each other in absolute disbelief that physics allowed that to happen.”

Firing a .50 BMG McMillan TAC-50 from a high-rise rooftop during the 2017 siege of Mosul, Alexander and his spotter smashed the previous world record by more than 1,000 meters—saving dozens of allied troops pinned down below.

Waiting ten full seconds for a bullet to cross the sky and strike an enemy position over two miles away pushes the boundaries of human precision and physics.

A #Marine infantry battalion that was embroiled in a war-zone scandal will present a former squad leader with the nation's third-highest valor award this week — nearly five years after he led his comrades out of an intense firefight in Afghanistan.

Former Sgt. Matthew Parker, who served as a squad leader with 3rd Battalion, 2nd Marines, during the unit's 2011 deployment to Afghanistan, will be presented with the Silver Star on Friday during a ceremony at #CampLejeune, North Carolina, Marine Corps Times has learned.

Parker is being recognized for stepping up to lead his platoon when his commander and another squad leader were injured in an attack while operating in Helmand province's Musa Qala district, according to his award citation.

While Parker's actions serve as an example of the success 3/2 showed on the battlefield during what was highly held as a successful deployment, much of it was overshadowed when a video surfaced in 2012 showing other Marines with his unit defiling enemy remains.

Parker was not involved, but his award nomination — along with several other personnel matters within the unit — was put on administrative hold, said 1st Lt. Joe Caldwell, a Marine spokesman.

The award then had to go through the approval process, Caldwell added. Parker's Silver Star was approved by Commandant Gen. Robert Neller on Dec. 31.

On May 21, 2011, Parker and his platoon were attacked by an entrenched enemy force. The insurgents were armed with small arms, machine guns, anti-tank-style weapons and grenade launchers.

When the Marines' platoon commander and another squad leader were injured in the attack, Parker sprang into action.
"Sergeant Parker boldly assumed control as the ground force commander of two rifle squads, a combined anti-armor team section, a vehicle mobile element and a sniper team," the award citation states.

Under a barrage of enemy fire, Parker coordinated the platoon's maneuvers until they were able to strike the enemy from three directions. When the insurgents hit back with intense machine gun and recoilless rifle fire, Parker "calmly and precisely coordinated for close-air support and high-mobility artillery rocket system strikes that destroyed two enemy machine gun positions," his citation states.

He seized that opportunity to guide supporting fires while continuing to direct his Marines. As a result, the enemy was forced to withdraw.

Parker helped evacuate the wounded Marines, despite continued sporadic fire from the insurgents as they withdrew. He led the Marines to safety at the closest patrol base.
"By his zealous initiative, courageous actions and exceptional dedication to duty, Sergeant Parker reflected great credit upon himself and upheld the highest traditions of the Marine Corps and the United States Naval Service," his citation states.

Parker was not the only member of 3/2 to be nominated for a valor award during that deployment. One of the snipers involved in the controversial video was put up for a Bronze Star with combat device, but that award has never been issued.
That Marine's sniper platoon was credited with killing hundreds of insurgents and integrating tanks into their missions — a highly successful move outside of normal sniper doctrine. The Corps' top leaders visited the team downrange that fall to congratulate the Marines on their accomplishments.

Parker could not immediately be reached for comment about his award. He medically retired from the #MarineCorps in February 2015, according to a Marine official.

KHILLIGAY, Afghanistan – U.S. Army Sgt. Joshua R. Labbe of the 10th Mountain Division's 1st Brigade Combat Team received the Silver Star medal, the nation's third highest award for valor in combat, on Feb. 16, during a ceremony at Forward Operating Base Khilligay in northern Afghanistan.

Labbe, from Stonington, Conn., an infantry squad leader with 1st Battalion, 87th Infantry Regiment, is credited with saving the life of one soldier and protecting numerous soldiers during a complex attack that lasted more than six hours.

“We are here to recognize the sacrifice and courage of the soldiers and leaders in Shafi Khel on Oct. 6,” said Lt. Col. Russell Lewis, 1-87 commander, said during the ceremony. “Sgt. Labbe is a hero. He didn't go out on Oct. 6 to earn an award — he just did his job. Except his job that day called for extraordinary actions and he stepped up and helped his comrades.”

On Oct. 6, 2010, Labbe's platoon was conducting a joint combat patrol in the village of Shafi Khel, Baghlan province, Afghanistan, with their Afghan national security force partners.

While establishing an observation post on a hilltop, Labbe and soldiers from 1st Squad as well as the mortar team, came under enemy fire. Initially, the enemy attacked the soldiers of 3rd Platoon with rocket-propelled grenades.
“One truck of ours was hit by an RPG,” Labbe said. “When I saw that truck get hit, I immediate started suppressing with the mortar system.”

Over the next four hours, the platoon came under RPG and small arms fire. Labbe directed the soldiers on the hill to return fire with multiple weapons systems. The hilltop then came under sniper fire, forcing Labbe and the other soldiers to take cover in holes they had dug.

Later, Labbe was told to collapse their position on the hilltop and return to the base of the hill where the remainder of his platoon was located.

“I had to get out of my hole and run to the other hole where the mortar system was,” he said. “When I got to the hole, I got everyone one up, got them online, and got everybody ready. As soon as we got out of the hole, we got sniper fire again.”

With three of the five soldiers making it across the hill to the other hole safely, Labbe and Pfc. Parker Radatz had returned to the mortar hole due to the accuracy of the sniper fire. Labbe and Radatz gathered themselves and attempted to get across the hill again.

“I ran to my hole thinking he was right beside me; little did I know he had actually tripped and fell,” Labbe said. “I turned around, and I saw him trying to get his composure to get back up, but he couldn't because there were multiple rounds impacting all around him.”

With complete disregard for his own safety, Labbe ran across the exposed hilltop to the fallen soldier through enemy fire, picked him up, and brought him to safety.

“I just did what I had to in that situation,” Labbe said. “He has people that care for him and love him, I knew I had to go pick him up and get him to safety. It's my job to take care of my men.”

Later, as the platoon moved down the road, the tow bar pulling the battle-damaged vehicle snapped. While Labbe and three soldiers began repairing the tow bar, once again, the platoon came under small arms fire from nearby rooftops and walls. Labbe immediately returned fire with his M4 rifle.

The small arms fire discontinued for a moment, allowing Labbe to run back to his vehicle to retrieve an M249 machine gun. He moved to a position allowing him to pull security down the alleyway and the walls where they had received fire. At this point, the enemy hopped over the walls and began engaging the platoon again.

With the enemy less than 20 meters away, Labbe stood completely exposed on the road and continued to shield the recovery crew as he fired the machine gun from his shoulder. After expending the 200-round ammunition pouch, he fired the weapon using his 30-round M4 rifle magazines.

“I engaged them for roughly two minutes and continued to pull security until the tow bar was fixed,” he said.

Once the vehicle was recovered, 3rd Platoon continued down the road, where they were ambushed. While still in close contact with the enemy, another vehicle suddenly plunged into an irrigation ditch. Labbe immediately dismounted and moved under fire to the stuck vehicle.

He coordinated the evacuation and recovery of the vehicle while still being engaged with RPG and machinegun fire from compounds and tree lines from less than 100 meters away. Labbe remained exposed to the enemy until the rest of the platoon recovered the vehicle and mounted back in their trucks.

“I feel honored to receive the Silver Star,” he said. “However, I don't think just my actions alone allowed us to be victorious that day. It was the whole platoon. Everyone who was out there that day played an important role in getting everyone back here alive. I couldn't have done what I did that day without my brothers in 3rd Platoon.”

Over the course of more than six hours of close combat, Labbe went above and beyond the call of duty as a squad leader.

“Today, we recognize his actions because they are not common,” said Lewis. “His actions that day distinguished him from others and truly impacted the outcome of the fight in Shafi Khel.”

The President of the United States of America, authorized by Title 10, Section 8742, U.S.C., awards the Air Force Cross to Senior Airman Jason D. Cunningham for extraordinary heroism in military operations against an opposing armed force while serving as a pararescueman near the village of Marzak in the Paktia Province of Afghanistan on 4 March 2002.

On that proud day, Airman Cunningham was the primary Air Force Combat Search and Rescue medic assigned to a Quick Reaction Force tasked to recover two American servicemen evading capture in austere terrain occupied by massed Al Qaida and Taliban forces.

Shortly before landing, his MH-47E helicopter received accurate rocket-propelled grenade and small arms fire, severely disabling the aircraft and causing it to crash land. The assault force formed a hasty defense and immediately suffered three fatalities and five critical casualties.

Despite effective enemy fire, and at great risk to his own life, Airman Cunningham remained in the burning fuselage of the aircraft in order to treat the wounded. As he moved his patients to a more secure location, mortar rounds began to impact within fifty feet of his position. Disregarding this extreme danger, he continued the movement and exposed himself to enemy fire on seven separate occasions.

When the second casualty collection point was also compromised, in a display of uncommon valor and gallantry, Airman Cunningham braved an intense small arms and rocket-propelled grenade attack while repositioning the critically wounded to a third collection point. Even after he was mortally wounded and quickly deteriorating, he continued to direct patient movement and transferred care to another medic.

In the end, his distinct efforts led to the successful delivery of ten gravely wounded Americans to life-saving medical treatment. Through his extraordinary heroism, superb airmanship, aggressiveness in the face of the enemy, and in the dedication of his service to his country, Senior Airman Cunningham reflected the highest credit upon himself and the United States #AirForce.

Small-arms fire rained down on the men of Company F, 2nd Battalion, 23rd Marines. Both Iraqi civilians and Marines were injured. Pinned down, with the injured needing assistance, Sgt. Scott C. Montoya rushed through enemy fire while "repeatedly exposing himself to fire-swept streets," according to his Navy Cross award citation.

Montoya received the U.S. military's second-highest award at Camp Pendleton for heroism stemming from his actions on April 8, 2003, two weeks into Operation Iraqi Freedom.

With his firearm in one hand engaging the enemy and a badly bleeding Marine in the other, he fought their way 500 yards to safety. He returned to the crossfire again and dragged another - who'd been dazed by the concussion of a grenade blast - to a casualty collection point. In all, he rescued four injured Marines and one Iraqi civilian out of harm's way, according to his citation.

Montoya's "extraordinary heroism" arose out of the battle for Baghdad.

Montoya described it this way:

"I saw a hurt Marine, and all my training came into play. It wasn't a cognitive thing; I just saw the situation and cared for my Marines."
Sgt. Jose N. Sanchez, a supply clerk with 2/23, has known Montoya for six years and wasn't surprised when he heard the news.

"The level he went - it's above and beyond the call of anyone, even a Marine," Sanchez said, adding: "What matters to him are his Marines, not the awards or the actions he took."

Montoya received the award in front of family, friends, and the men of his unit. Orange County Sheriff Michael S. Carona was also present.

A deputy sheriff in Orange County, Montoya drew praise from many of his co-workers - including Carona.
"He is a complete warrior," Carona said.

"Whether as a Marine or as a law enforcement figure, he is always putting the community or the country above his own personal safety."

Carona alluded to Montoya's rapid response under fire.

"These things happen in the blink of a second, and an individual has to decide to be a hero or not. He decided to be one."

In the end, Montoya said, “It's just a medal.”

"Service before self is something I teach in the Marine Corps Martial Arts Program," continued Montoya, a MCMAP instructor for his unit. "I feel the award represents the character of the Corps."

Col. Geffery L. Cooper, the battalion's commanding officer during Operation Iraqi Freedom, said Montoya's award was well-deserved.

"It means a great deal to me that the Corps can recognize such Marines of valor in combat,” said Cooper. (Montoya) is a man of integrity and leadership, and his loyalty is unquestionable. He is a great example and advocate for all reservists.”
